qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: North American Stainless (NAS) possesses a favorable regional cost position, but the business operates as a cyclical commodity price-taker lacking pricing power above inflation across the cycle. Margins are dictated by global stainless base prices, scrap/nickel surcharges, and Chinese overcapacity; FY2025 swung to a net loss of -€40M with ROCE averaging well below the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Commodity stainless steel price-taker subject to severe cyclical margin swings and global/Chinese overcapacity. 5-year average ROCE is ~9% and FY2025 swung to a net loss of -€40M; profit engine NAS relies heavily on US tariff protection rather than a structural customer moat.
qualitative.evidence: Reported ROCE fell to 9.0% in FY2024, and FY2025 recorded a net loss of -€40M on €5.78B revenue due to depressed stainless base prices, European weakness, and inventory write-downs. Net debt expanded to €1.2B following the €820M acquisition of Haynes International. Stainless steel base prices and alloy surcharges fluctuate directly with underlying commodity quotes, demonstrating zero independent pricing power.
